flags.summary: The sales manager instructed a setter to apply harder financial qualification to prospects based on their country of origin, naming Egypt as a country to qualify harder and UAE as one to qualify less.
evidence: Andrew Jin: it's just a hunch. He probably won't have money, but taking, like, a firefighter in UAE, that's... he's not gonna be earning a lot... Like, yesterday, I had a guy from Egypt. Definitely, he didn't have the money, yeah? So I don't know, can we...

Chris Klevan: Here's what I would say, if they come from certain, like, UAE is one of those countries where I probably wouldn't hard financially qualify too much, if somebody's coming from Egypt, yeah, I probably would, you know, like, let them know the, little bit harder about the investment, Kim, I would do that a little bit more, and just so that way they're aware.
Chris Klevan: if you have somebody from countries that it might be harder for them to afford things, just like, let them know, you know, just kind of give them a little bit of a harder, for FQ.

Chris Klevan, to Andrew, immediately after: with fitness, you never really know somebody's situation until you know their situation. So I would just kind of like take the call, see what happens, try not to assume anything.

flags.summary: A prospect wrote in to say he felt pushed and that his disclosure about his father had been used on him, and no-showed the follow-up; the closer's own summary was that he had burned him.
evidence: Andrew Jin: Manny yesterday didn't show up... And he basically said that he didn't like, at the end, that he felt pushed and used the emotions about his father and so on. Yeah, so I technically burned him, but...
Andrew Jin: when I asked him, it wasn't like he could just dodge me, and then, like, he sent, like, a really long text explaining, like, what felt good, what felt bad
Chris Klevan: Now we know. You got the feedback... just got to do a better job of isolating the right objection and understanding where the person's coming from.

For the underlying call see 2026-06-08_manny-nunez_andrew-musial, where the rep pushed financing three times after explicit refusals and returned to the prospect's father and diabetes after the price objection.

flags.summary: Closers were coached to take a card on file from prospects who have declined to be charged, with the manager noting that once the card is held it can simply be run.
evidence: Chris Klevan: Even if it's like a credit card commitment, even if they're like, I cannot run money, be like, cool, then we'll just take down the card on file and I won't run it until this day.
Chris Klevan: That's the worst case scenario, though. Like, get a commitment. Get something. Because once the card's on file, we can technically just run it. So.
Chris Klevan: From now on, if you get any logistical moving money around, get a deposit.

flags.summary: A mandatory deposit was introduced as standing policy for onboarding calls, follow-up calls, spouse objections and any payment delay — a charge outside the two stated tiers, exampled at $100 and described to prospects as refundable.
evidence: Chris Klevan: moving forward, no onboarding calls go on the calendar unless we take a deposit.

Chris Klevan: So no worries that you got to move some money around. Here's what we'll do. We'll just do a small deposit. This way, we can go ahead... So we'll just do a refundable deposit and get you walked and loaded from there.

Chris Klevan: The reason we do the deposit is because we don't book any follow-up calls or onboarding calls or anything with anybody unless they do it, because it takes away from someone else being able to book. So we have to reserve our time because we get super busy.
Chris Klevan: if they say yes, then you know, cool. It's a hundred bucks. Let's do it. Or whatever.

Chris Klevan: So deposits. From now on, if you get spouse objections, deposits... If you're doing a follow-up call with somebody, check and make sure that they're actually going to show to the next call by getting a deposit. Deposits, deposits, deposits.

flags.summary: Closers were coached to deliberately withhold the deposit amount in order to provoke a reaction from the prospect and then use that reaction against them.
evidence: Chris Klevan: I actually like to not tell them what the deposit is going to be and then see if they react terribly to it. And then I say, dude, like I could have told you it was $1. Like what's going on?
Ben Byrne: Yeah. Classic.
Chris Klevan: Yeah. That's my favorite. They always look at me like, damn, you're right. You got me.

flags.summary: Closers were coached to argue that a price the prospect finds financially uncomfortable is itself the reason to pay it, in direct tension with the manager's own stated rule not to sell to anyone it would put in a tight spot.
evidence: Chris Klevan: if you invested $6,000 on something and you're working with the best coach that you can invest in, every single time you open up your bank account, what do you think you're going to be more likely to follow through with, something that you paid $6,000 for or something that you paid $2,000 for?

Chris Klevan: the fact that it's $6,000 is actually the reason you should pay it because if you're super uncomfortable about it, you're going to [follow] through. You want to get your money's worth. $2,000 is easy for you, then you're going to follow through.
Chris Klevan: Every time you look at your bank account, use that as 6,000 reasons to actually follow through with it.
Chris Klevan, six minutes earlier: I only sell people if I know for sure they can afford it and it's not going to put them in a tight spot.

flags.summary: A 'performance guarantee' is treated as an official closing instrument to be deployed against price objections, while its terms, duration, remedy and refund position were never stated on this call or on any sales call in this batch.
evidence: Andrew Jin: Would you bring up also the performance guarantee at that point? — Chris Klevan: Yeah, I would. I would bring it up. We're literally guaranteeing it.

Chris Klevan: when it comes to the kettlebell space, when it comes to working with the best, when it comes to guaranteeing the results like we do, Trevor's the best, and that's why the investment is what it is.

For contrast, on 2026-06-08_kareem-shirazi_andrew-musial_2 a prospect asked directly whether a 30-day guarantee existed and was answered with an 8 kg kettlebell strength promise instead, with refund terms never stated before he paid $6,000.

flags.summary: Prospects communicate with an AI chat bot inside the sales flow and reps do not reliably see those messages — a prospect's notice that he would not attend a booked follow-up went unread.
evidence: Andrew Jin: Manny yesterday didn't show up, but, well, he actually texted also the, our AI chat bot, and I didn't see that.
Andrew Jin: I checked the sales kick, he messaged our AI bot that, I already know everything from the first call, I only need to know the price.
Chris Klevan: never leave. If somebody sends you a message or anything, even if it's, like, technically negative, don't just, like, ignore it. Make sure to respond.
